hints: Notice both pH values are well above 7, so think about which type of Group 2 compound can actually release hydroxide ions in water.
Sulfates like $\text{BaSO}_4$ and $\text{MgSO}_4$ do not produce $\text{OH}^-$ ions, so they cannot give pH 13.6 or 9.4.
For Group 2 hydroxides, solubility increases down the group, so connect higher solubility to higher $\text{OH}^-$ concentration and higher pH for V.
walkthrough:
**Use pH to identify the type of compound**

Both solutions are alkaline, pH 13.6 and pH 9.4. That tells us lots of $\text{OH}^-$ ions must be present.

$$\text{M(OH)}_2(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{M}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{OH}^-(aq)$$

**Rule out the sulfates**

$\text{BaSO}_4$ is virtually insoluble and $\text{MgSO}_4$ dissolves to give a neutral solution. Neither releases $\text{OH}^-$, so neither can give a strongly alkaline pH.

**Apply the Group 2 hydroxide solubility trend**

Group 2 hydroxides become more soluble down the group. So $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is much more soluble than $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$.

More dissolved solid means higher $[\text{OH}^-]$ and higher pH.

**Match V and W**

V has the very high pH of 13.6, so it must be the more soluble hydroxide, the barium compound. W has the lower pH of 9.4, so it must be the sparingly soluble hydroxide, the magnesium compound.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{BaSO}_4$ is insoluble and $\text{MgSO}_4$ gives an approximately neutral solution. Neither can produce pH 13.6 or 9.4 because no $\text{OH}^-$ is released.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the same sulfate problem reversed. $\text{MgSO}_4$ is soluble but neutral, and $\text{BaSO}_4$ is insoluble, so neither explains a strongly alkaline solution.
options.C: Correct. Both are hydroxides so both give alkaline solutions. $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is far more soluble than $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$, giving a much higher $[\text{OH}^-]$ and therefore the higher pH of 13.6 for V, with $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ giving pH 9.4 for W.
options.D: Incorrect. This has the right compounds but the wrong way round. $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is sparingly soluble and cannot give pH 13.6, while $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is too soluble to give only pH 9.4.
